Debugging Odin scripts

Native code and supported debugging tools#

odin_godot compiles Odin scripts ahead of time into a native library (.dylib/.so/.dll) loaded through GDExtension. Inspect script execution with logging and a native debugger. Godot's script-line debugger does not interpret or step through this code:

Tool Works for Odin scripts?
Godot in-editor breakpoints (gutter dots) ❌ No, there is no interpreter to halt (use Tools > Debug Game (Break at Cursor))
Godot step / pause / resume of script lines ❌ No; lldb steps natively instead
Godot expression evaluation in the debugger panel ❌ No
Godot remote scene tree / live property edit ✅ Yes (engine-side, not script-line)
gd.print / gd.error / gd.warn logging ✅ Yes; output appears in the terminal and editor as described below
native lldb (line breakpoints, stepping, bt, frame variable) ✅ Yes; inspects compiled script execution
crash backtraces (signal 11) with Odin proc names ✅ Yes, built with -debug, symbols present

The engine calls an Odin procedure through a compiled C-ABI function pointer, outside GDScript's bytecode VM. Use logging to trace behavior, lldb to inspect live execution, and native backtraces to locate crashes.

Crash reports in the editor#

The editor's Output dock receives the child game's push_error/print messages over Godot's TCP debugger channel. It does not capture the child's stderr. Launch the editor from a terminal to see stderr reports; an editor launched from Finder has no visible terminal for them. odin_godot reports panics and fatal signals through different paths:

  • Odin panic / failed assert (including failed type assertions): the script context's assertion proc (runtime/panic_native.odin) prints ODIN_SCRIPT_PANIC <prefix>: <message> (file:line:col) to stderr and sends it through push_error. The editor Output displays that line in red with the script location:

    Code
    ERROR: ODIN_SCRIPT_PANIC panic: no Hud attached (res://scripts/hud.odin:41:2)

  • Fatal signal (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL/SIGFPE, typically from calling an engine method on a nil object handle): a crash reporter (core/crash.odin, macOS + Linux; installed only in the game process, never the editor) prints to stderr:

    Code
    ODIN_GODOT_CRASH: fatal signal SIGSEGV — crash in native code (Odin script or engine).
ODIN_GODOT_CRASH at   pc 0x…  my_scripts::take_damage + 0x20  (…/libodinscripts.dylib)
ODIN_GODOT_CRASH from lr 0x…  my_scripts::[odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin]::_enemy_m_on_hit + 0xac  (…)
ODIN_GODOT_CRASH backtrace (backtrace_symbols_fd):
0   libodin_godot.dylib   0x… core::[crash.odin]::crash_handler + 496
1   libodinscripts.dylib  0x… my_scripts::[odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin]::_enemy_m_on_hit + 172
2   Godot                 0x… _ZN6Object5callpE… + 184
…

    The at pc line identifies the faulting Odin procedure from the signal context, since stack walkers lose that frame across the signal trampoline. The reporter then attempts to send one red summary to the editor Output ("Odin: the game CRASHED in native code (SIGSEGV …)") and re-raises the signal for Godot's crash handler, which prints the engine backtrace.

The child game inherits stderr from a terminal-launched editor. Headless test harnesses can capture it directly. Within the editor GUI, use the push_error lines for the summary and script location.

To resolve a bare module + offset line to source, use the .dSYM kept beside the library:

Shell
atos -o bin/libodinscripts.dylib.dSYM/Contents/Resources/DWARF/libodinscripts.dylib \
     -l <module load address> <pc address>

(on Linux: addr2line -f -e bin/libodinscripts.so <offset>). This is usually unnecessary, since the Odin frames come out symbolized already, as above.

Stack overflows, traps, and exported crash logs#

The crash handler uses sigaltstack to report stack overflows; Windows uses SetThreadStackGuarantee. It also handles traps after panic, assert, and bounds failures (SIGTRAP/SIGILL; Windows: EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT). A bounds failure's index/range message goes only to stderr, so rerun from a terminal or under lldb to read it. Exported games write the report to user://odin_crash.log for post-mortem diagnosis. The Windows SEH reporter in core/crash_windows.odin uses DbgHelp with the build's .pdbs; it is compile-verified and still requires a run on Windows.

The mid-crash push_error may not reach the editor if the debugger link closes first. Use stderr or the crash file for the full report.

Verified end-to-end by tests/crash/run.sh (sentinel CRASH_TEST_OK): panic, segv, stack overflow, editor surfacing, and a real exported-.app crash.

Launching the debugger from the editor (macOS + Linux)#

Three items under Project > Tools configure common lldb launch tasks, including paths, SIP re-signing, and breakpoint syntax:

  • Debug Game (LLDB): opens a terminal running the game under lldb and starts it immediately. Script panic/failed assert stops at the panic site with the stack available for inspection. A hard crash, such as SIGSEGV from a nil handle, stops at the faulting instruction.
  • Debug Game (Break at Cursor): put the caret on a line in an .odin script, choose this item, and the game stops when it reaches the line, with locals available. This sets a native breakpoint; engine gutter dots apply to the GDScript VM.
  • Generate VS Code Debug Config: writes .vscode/launch.json + tasks.json so F5 in VS Code (with the CodeLLDB extension) debugs the game with clickable breakpoints, stepping, and a live Variables pane, directly in your .odin files.

All three use addons/odin_godot/build/debug_game.sh, which also works standalone (see §2), and select the same Godot executable as the editor's Play command. On Windows, only Generate VS Code Debug Config is available. It writes a cppvsdbg launch.json (the standard C/C++ extension) that debugs the editor's binary directly against the .pdbs the builds emit; no re-signing needed there.

JetBrains IDEs (Rider, CLion, IDEA Ultimate, …)#

For editing in JetBrains IDEs, install the Odin Support plugin. Run Project > Tools > Generate ols.json (IDE Completion) in Godot, then right-click the generated ols.json in the IDE and use the plugin's import action. It configures the godot collection (the addon), the Odin core collections, and the checker args that keep @(gd_method) markers from being flagged. Editors using ols, such as Neovim, Zed, Sublime, or Helix, can use the same file.

Debugging support depends on the IDE:

  • Rider: the Odin plugin does not support debugging on Rider ≥ 2025.2, and Rider's own Native Executable run configurations run but cannot debug native code. Edit in Rider; debug via the Godot menu items above (terminal lldb) or the VS Code config.
  • CLion / IDEA Ultimate / GoLand / RustRover (+ the Native Debugging Support plugin where applicable): the Odin plugin uses LLDB on macOS/Linux. Point a run configuration at the debuggable Godot copy (get its path with build/debug_game.sh --prepare-only; macOS needs this re-signed copy because SIP blocks debugging the stock binary), with program arguments --path /path/to/your/project. Breakpoints in .odin files then bind normally. The godot_lldb.py pretty-printers are terminal/VS-Code-lldb extras; JetBrains' debugger does not load them.

1. Logging and errors: gd.print / gd.error / gd.warn#

Logging helpers live in godot/Ergonomics_Debug.odin, mirrored in bindgen/upstream/godot/ so they survive binding regeneration. They convert cstring -> String -> Variant -> gd_* in a single call:

Odin
import gd "godot:godot"

gd.print("player ready")          // -> stdout + the editor Output panel
gd.print_int(score)               // i64
gd.print_float(delta)             // f64
gd.print_bool(on_floor)           // bool
gd.print_value(some_variant)      // any Variant, stringified like GDScript print()

gd.warn("coin value was 0, defaulting to 1")   // yellow, non-fatal (push_warning)
gd.error("Hud node missing")      // red in Output/Debugger, with script context (push_error)

gd.error routes through Godot's push_error, so it shows in red in the editor Output and Debugger with the originating context, and is delivered to any attached debugger. Use it for genuine fault conditions; use gd.print for tracing.

Formatted output#

The helpers are contextless and do not import core:fmt, avoiding that dependency in wasm/web builds that do not need formatting. For formatted output, call Odin's core:fmt first, then print:

Odin
import "core:fmt"
import gd "godot:godot"

gd.print(fmt.ctprintf("score=%d at %v", score, self.owner_pos))  // ctprintf -> cstring (temp-allocated)
gd.print_str(fmt.tprintf("hp=%d/%d", hp, max_hp))                // tprintf -> string; print_str takes a string

ctprintf returns a temp-allocated cstring (freed at the next free_all(context.temp_allocator)), which is exactly what gd.print wants. tprintf returns a temp string, which you pass to gd.print_str / gd.error_str / gd.warn_str.

2. Native debugging with lldb#

The script library uses -debug -use-single-module (see atomic_odin_dll in build/common.sh) to provide named procedure symbols and DWARF data for line tables, typed arguments, and struct layouts. With Odin's default separate-modules debug build, macOS ld emits a one-entry debug map and dsymutil produces a near-empty .dSYM: procedure symbols remain, but line breakpoints, stepping, and frame variable do not work. The single-module build provides the debug information those operations require.

Use the launcher to debug Odin procedures with source lines (the same one the Project > Tools menu items run; --break accepts file.odin:LINE or a symbol regex, repeatable, and implies auto-run):

Shell
build/debug_game.sh tests/showcase                                # interactive (lldb) prompt
build/debug_game.sh --break player.odin:51 tests/showcase        # halt at that line
build/debug_game.sh --break coin_collect tests/showcase -- --headless --script test_showcase.gd

At the prompt: run (if not auto-run), then bt, n/s/c to step, frame variable to inspect. The launcher also auto-loads build/godot_lldb.py (lldb type summaries so godot.String / String_Name / Variant display their live values instead of an opaque pointer) and pre-sets a breakpoint on the script assertion proc, so a script panic("...") stops execution at the panic site for inspection.

macOS breakpoint matching and debugger permissions#

  1. Breakpoint syntax: use a regex, not the qualified name. lldb parses :: as a C++ qualified name and fails to bind b showcase_scripts::coin_collect (it stays "pending, 0 locations"). A regex breakpoint binds and fires:

    Code
    (lldb) break set -r coin_collect          # ✅ binds + fires
(lldb) b showcase_scripts::coin_collect   # ❌ stays pending, never hits

    The dll is dlopen'd at runtime, so the breakpoint is "pending" until Godot loads it. That is normal; lldb resolves it automatically on load.

  2. SIP blocks attaching to the installed Godot. The system Godot is code-signed without the get-task-allow entitlement, so debugserver refuses:

    Code
    error: process exited with status -1 (attach failed (Not allowed to attach to process...))

    The fix (which build/debug_game.sh does automatically, cached, without touching your install): make a copy of the Godot binary and ad-hoc re-sign it with get-task-allow:

    Shell
    cp /Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot /tmp/Godot-dbg
codesign --remove-signature /tmp/Godot-dbg
codesign --force --sign - --entitlements get-task-allow.entitlements /tmp/Godot-dbg

    where the entitlements plist sets com.apple.security.get-task-allow to true. The re-signed binary can run the project headless under the debugger. (Inside the Nix shell, /usr/bin/lldb is an xcrun shim that breaks because Nix points DEVELOPER_DIR at an SDK with no lldb; the launcher resets DEVELOPER_DIR to a real Xcode/CLT install.)

Example: a breakpoint hit#

In the showcase, a line breakpoint stops execution during a physics coin collection. lldb lists the source line, native call chain, and named procedure arguments with their current values:

Code
(lldb) breakpoint set -f coin.odin -l 50
Breakpoint 1: no locations (pending).        # normal: the dll isn't dlopen'd yet
(lldb) run
1 location added to breakpoint 1             # bound when Godot loaded the scripts dll
Process … stopped
* thread #1, stop reason = breakpoint 1.1
    frame #0: libodinscripts.dylib`showcase_scripts::coin_collect(self=0x…, body=0x…) at coin.odin:50:2
   48       if self.taken {return}
   49       self.taken = true
-> 50       game_state_add(self.value)
(lldb) bt
* frame #0: libodinscripts.dylib`showcase_scripts::coin_collect(...) at coin.odin:50:2
  frame #1: libodinscripts.dylib`showcase_scripts::[odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin]::_coin_m_collect(...) at odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin:…
  frame #2: libodin_godot.dylib`core::[instance.odin]::inst_call + 520
  frame #3: Godot`Object::callp(...) + 184
  frame #4: Godot`Object::emit_signalp(...) + 1568
  …

Inspecting self, arguments, locals#

frame variable shows the typed arguments; dereference self (C syntax: *self, not Odin's self^) for the whole live script struct:

Code
(lldb) frame variable
(showcase_scripts::Player *) self = 0x0000600000c71b70
(f64) delta = 0.066456
(lldb) frame variable *self
(showcase_scripts::Player) *self = (owner = …, speed = 500)
(lldb) target variable left_name          # file-scope globals: `target variable`
(godot::String_Name) left_name = StringName("ui_left")   # <- godot_lldb.py summary

Locals become available after their declarations execute; use next to step past them. If a value is unavailable because execution stopped in the prologue or an optimized frame, inspect registers and memory. arm64 passes the first integer arguments in x0/x1, so use register read x0, then memory read on the pointer.

3. Reading a crash backtrace (signal 11)#

When an Odin script segfaults, the process dies with SIGSEGV (signal 11). Because the dll carries symbols, you get the Odin proc names directly: run the crashing scenario under lldb (it stops at the fault automatically) and bt:

Code
Process … stopped
* thread #1, stop reason = EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x0)
    frame #0: libodinscripts.dylib`my_scripts::take_damage + 44
(lldb) bt
* frame #0: libodinscripts.dylib`my_scripts::take_damage + 44
  frame #1: libodinscripts.dylib`my_scripts::[odin_godot_scripts.gen.odin]::_enemy_m_on_hit + 120
  frame #2: libodin_godot.dylib`core::[instance.odin]::inst_call + 448
  frame #3: Godot`Object::emit_signalp(...) + 1568
  …

The top frame (my_scripts::take_damage + 44) is the faulting Odin proc; the +44 is the byte offset into it. Use image lookup --address <pc> for the source line, or disassemble --frame to see the faulting instruction. Without lldb, a crash still prints a native backtrace to stderr that includes these symbol names. Grep it for your package name (my_scripts::).

A no-lldb alternative for repeatable crashes: macOS writes a .ips crash report under ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/; its "Thread N Crashed" backtrace contains the same libodinscripts.dylib <pkg>::<proc> + <off> lines.

4. Native stack info: _debug_get_current_stack_info#

OdinLanguage implements the _debug_get_current_stack_info script-language virtual by capturing a native backtrace (core/debug.odin). When called, it:

  1. Walks the native stack with libunwind's _Unwind_Backtrace.
  2. Resolves each return address with dladdr → dli_sname (e.g. showcase_scripts::coin_collect) + dli_fname (the dll path).
  3. Keeps frames from the scripts library and returns Godot's expected structure: Array[ Dictionary{ "function": String, "line": int, "source": String } ].

Full backtraces with omitted frame pointers#

Odin omits frame pointers and has no flag to retain them. In the test below, execinfo's frame-pointer backtrace() therefore returns only the innermost frame. _Unwind_Backtrace uses DWARF/compact-unwind tables, as lldb does, to recover the call chain without frame pointers. tests/debug/bt_probe.odin verifies this difference (backtrace() = 1 frame vs _Unwind_Backtrace = the whole chain).

Line numbers are 0#

Mapping an address to a source line needs DWARF line-table resolution at runtime (an addr2line/libdwarf step), which this implementation does not provide. It reports "line": 0 and uses the library path as "source". Function names are resolved; source lines are unavailable. Use lldb for source-line resolution.

When Godot requests stack information#

When called mid-script, native capture returns Odin frames such as showcase_scripts::coin_collect, as tested under "Verification" below. Godot invokes _debug_get_current_stack_info during an active remote-debug session, when EngineDebugger reports an error or breakpoint to a connected debugger.

A plain gd.error does not automatically add the Odin stack to editor Output. In tests/debug/run.sh part C, the showcase runs headless with ODIN_DEBUG_STACK_DUMP=1; the engine does not call the virtual:

Code
== (C) integration: does Godot invoke _debug_get_current_stack_info in a normal run? ==
  RESULT: Godot did NOT call _debug_get_current_stack_info in this headless run.

The virtual returns a well-formed Array containing the Odin call chain when invoked. It does not provide an automatic script-line stack for plain errors or crashes in the editor. Use lldb bt (section 2/3) for routine stack inspection.

backtrace()/dladdr are POSIX-ish and present on darwin/linux. Windows and the web/wasm build use a stub that returns an empty Array (core/debug_other.odin).

5. Web / wasm builds#

In the browser there is no dlopen, no native stack to walk, and no lldb. Debug web builds with logging (gd.print → the JS console) and the browser devtools. The native stack-info capture is stubbed to empty on wasm. See docs/exporting.md.

Verification#

tests/debug/run.sh, included in tests/run_all.sh with sentinel DEBUG_OK, checks native capture, lldb integration, and whether Godot requests stack info:

  • (A) unit: tests/debug/bt_probe.odin runs _Unwind_Backtrace + dladdr + the scripts-dll filter over its own call chain (prints bt_probe::sim_coin_collect | …) and dlopens the showcase library to confirm dladdr reports dli_sname=showcase_scripts::coin_collect, dli_fname=…/libodinscripts.dylib. → BTPROBE_OK.
  • (B) lldb: launches Godot under lldb, breaks on coin_collect, triggers a physics collection, and asserts stop reason = breakpoint plus the function in bt. → DEBUG_LLDB_OK. (Gated: skipped if lldb is unavailable.)
  • (C) integration: runs the showcase with ODIN_DEBUG_STACK_DUMP=1 and reports whether Godot actually called the virtual (it does not, outside remote-debug).

Run it: nix develop --command bash -c 'bash tests/debug/run.sh'.
